main_text.p: 2. Tenuisti manum dexteram meam) Hoc est, tu uires ad res praeclaras agendas & perficiendas, largitus es mihi: tu fuccessus concesfi-sti mihi: tu laboranti & periclitanti tulisti opem. Haec enim omnia phrasis illa hebraea, Tenere alicuius manum, significat.

§. Consilio tuo diriges me) Est vox spei, quum mihi hactenus re uere sacra, videlicet salutaris consilio mihi adfueris: spero te in posterum quoq; mihi consulturum esse. Hanc benedictionem diuina sibi gratulatur Dauid, dicens: Benedicam Iehouae, qui confuluit mihi etiā noctib. quib. erudiunt me renes mei, Psal.16.7.

4. Tandem in gloriam suscipies me) Deus aufert opprobrium & contemtum a feruis suis, Psal.119. & dat illis veram gloriam & gratiā. 84.11. Cauffa autē huius benedictionis expofita est nobili Epiphonemate illo: Honorantes me honorabo, contemnentes autē me contemnentur. 1.Sam.2.30.

page.notes: Running head and page number read as printed; "LXXXIII" is a best reading. The "§." before "Consilio" may be a verse sign; it is copied as it looks. The bare reference "84.11." stands at the left edge of the column, not clearly in the margin, so it is kept inline. The left-margin references "Leu.10." and "Maij 3." are hard to read and are doubtful abbreviations. "Psal.16.7" and "Psal.119" are copied as printed. The line "Quis mihi" is printed with a space before the question mark. Catchword "derio" is the start of the next line, placed at the lower right.
